tools.name: data_query
tools.title: Data query
tools.description: Structured, read-only query over ONE client's payroll and enriched calculation data (needs a client). Use it only for questions the fixed tools (client_eligibility, client_trend, client_at_risk, simulate and the rest) cannot answer: descriptive or comparative questions such as an average, a count or a total by location, month, year, designation or method. For anything about the credit figure, eligibility or what the engine concluded, the fixed tools are authoritative; this tool returns exact rows and aggregates from the data, it does not interpret them. Read data_catalog first and use its names exactly, never an invented column; use data_distinct_values to find a location or code before filtering on it. Name every measure with `as` (for example `average_headcount`): the answer refers to a result column by that name. Never write SQL. Prefer an aggregate to a long list: a result is capped (default 100 rows, at most 500) and says when it was cut. Rows that describe individual employees go to the person asking only; Copilot Cowork refuses them unless the user is a writer.

findings.title: Employee counted at two worksites in one month — clear-cut
findings.why_it_matters: The engine counts headcount per unit, so a person appearing at two worksites in the same month is counted twice. That inflates Average Headcount, which inflates the credit. In these one worksite holds at least 75% of the month's hours, so which unit owns the head is arithmetic rather than a judgement.

findings.why_it_matters: The engine counts headcount per unit, so a person appearing at two worksites in the same month is counted twice. That inflates Average Headcount, which inflates the credit.
